learning: Iteration 0 shows drift, not oscillation: steering_oscillation was 0.14 to 0.17 while max_error reached the 0.06 m limit. Check whether kp 6 reduces line_loss_events and max_error without raising steering_oscillation above about 0.25. If progress still stalls on the slalom, the next lever is the sensor span or sensor lead, not base_speed.
notes: Adopts the Builder's ±0.04 m sensor span with weights scaled to x/0.04. Raises kp to 6 and kd to 0.6 to correct the drift that ended every iteration-0 run off track, and trims base_speed to 1.5.
rationale: Iteration 0 (entityR2A) went off_track on every trial on all three development tracks. Progress was only 0.11 to 0.16, max_error sat at the 0.06 m off-track floor, and line_loss_events were 1 to 2 per run. steering_oscillation stayed low at 0.14 to 0.17. The robot is therefore drifting off the line because its correction is too weak, not because it is oscillating. I keep the Builder's widened sensor span (x = ±0.04 at 0.02 m spacing) and scale the sensor weights as x/0.04, so the weights stay -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1 and the signal range is unchanged. I raise kp from 4.0 to 6.0 to give the loop more correction authority, since the low oscillation suggests headroom. I raise kd from 0.3 to 0.6 to damp the extra gain at the 0.05 m sensor lead. I keep ki at 0.05 to avoid windup on the bends. I lower base_speed from 1.6 to 1.5 so the robot is less likely to leave the line on the sharper bends. Speed is not the limiting factor, because the runs failed early, not on time, but a small reduction gives the higher gain more room to correct. Expected result: fewer line-loss events, lower max_error, and more progress, with steering_oscillation staying below about 0.25. I cannot confirm this until the race runs. Body width cannot widen the off-track limit: the limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), and even body_width 0.18 gives only 0.0575, so the geometry stays as the Builder specified.
